facts.fact: The World Bank's concept document, prepared 26 April 2021, states that in rural areas the civil registration system is largely paper-based and relies on manual processes, and calls the civil registration process as a whole decentralised and largely paper-based.

The World Bank states that in the civil registration centres of urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire no standardised system is used and, with no shared digital platform, electronic civil registry records are stored locally and not consolidated.

The World Bank says digitisation is uneven across the civil registration centres of urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire and that rural areas are largely paper-based; it gives no count or share of centres.

The World Bank states that the Government of Congo has developed a civil registration digitalisation roadmap to standardise the systems and create a consolidated population register; the roadmap's date and cost are not given.
